 Dated this the 11th day of December, 2024  ORDER This Bail Application is filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
2.
Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.720/2024 of Ollur Police Station, Thrissur.

The above case is registered against the petitioner alleging offences punishable punishable under Section 420 and 406 IPC.
3.
The prosecution case is that on 19.05.2023 at 1:30 pm, the petitioner pledged 14.200 grams of spurious gold in Akshya Sree Gold Loan, an institution in which the defacto complainant is a partner.
The petitioner by pledging such spurious gold, availed Rs.2,02,400/- Hence, it is alleged that the accused committed the offence.
Heard counsel for the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor.

5. The counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner originally pledged the gold in another institution and the Akshaya Gold Loan Authorities said that they will take over the loan and clear the liability from the other Company.
Thereafter, the gold was taken and pledged in the defacto complainant's institution.
It is submitted that the allegation against the petitioner is not correct.
After verifying the gold through an appraiser, the gold was accepted and the loan was given.
The petitioner submitted that he has not any committed offence.
It is also submitted that in the other company namely Olari Maben Nidhi Ltd, already filed a complaint, which leads to Annexure-3 FIR and the petitioner was already released on bail in that case.
6. The Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
The Public Prosecutor submitted that the 2024:KER:93905 BAIL APPL. NO.9807 OF 2024 petitioner has got antecedents and he is involved in other case also.
7. After hearing both sides, I think the petitioner can be released on bail after imposing stringent conditions.
It is true that the allegation against the petitioner is serious.
But the prosecution case can be proved through documentary evidence.
Admittedly, the spurious document is now with the defacto complainant's institution.
Therefore, there is nothing to seize from the petitioner.

entities.text: Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant paragraph of the above judgment is extracted hereunder.
"12. We may note that personal liberty is an important aspect of our constitutional mandate.

The occasion to arrest an accused during investigation arises when custodial investigation becomes necessary or it is a heinous crime or where there is a possibility of influencing the witnesses or accused may abscond.
Merely because an arrest can be made because it is lawful does not mandate that arrest must be made.
A distinction must be made between the existence of the power to arrest and the justification for exercise of it.
(Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189: (1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981))

entities.text: Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189: (1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If arrest is made routine, it can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self-esteem of a person.

If the Investigating Officer has no reason to believe that the accused will abscond or disobey summons and has, in fact,
throughout cooperated with the investigation we fail to appreciate why there should be a compulsion on the officer to arrest the accused."
10.

In Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961], the Apex Court observed 2024:KER:93905 BAIL APPL. NO.9807 OF 2024 that even if the allegation is one of grave economic offence, it is not a rule that bail should be denied in every case.
Considering the dictum laid down in the above decision and considering the facts and circumstances of this case

, this Bail Application is allowed with the following directions:
1. The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within two weeks from today and shall undergo interrogation.
2. After interrogation, if the Investigating Officer propose to arrest the petitioner, she shall be released on bail on executing a bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the arresting officer concerned.
The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer for interrogation as and when required.

The petitioner shall co- operate with the investigation and shall not, directly or indirectly Bini vs State Of Kerala on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144579287/
3
make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
4. Petitioner shall not leave India without permission of the jurisdictional Court.

5. Petitioner shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which she is accused, or suspected,
of the commission of which she is suspected.

6. If any of the above conditions are violated by the petitioner, the jurisdictional 2024:KER:93905 BAIL APPL. NO.9807 OF 2024 Court can cancel the bail in accordance to law, even though the bail is granted by this Court.
The prosecution and the victim are at liberty to approach the jurisdictional Court to cancel the bail, if any of the above conditions are violated.
